## Summary

Follow-up to #337624.

- Automatically surface successful generated images in a **Generated Images** section of the Agents window's Artifacts pill, separate from other images and files. Preserve deduplication and removal behavior for explicitly recorded artifacts.
- Include generated image references and URI-backed user attachments in the conversation carousel. Open the originating chat's collection and preserve the clicked image even when gallery display names differ.
- Use canonical `.jpg` extensions and stable hash-suffixed generated-image filenames across previews, artifacts, the carousel, and Save. Referenced resource URIs remain unchanged.
- Prevent hidden turn summaries from adding a trailing gap when the response toolbar appears.
- Begin resizing immediately when image bytes are ready, skipping the initial loading wipe while preserving the remaining reveal's speed curve, reduced-motion/high-contrast behavior, and exact final dimensions.
- Show duration, actual image byte size, and a `Tokens -` placeholder in the expanded image-tool dropdown. Keep the metadata left-aligned with balanced padding; preserve Copilot execution durations in restored history.
- Let the existing chat pet paint at a small easel while an image tool runs, with matching Stable/Insiders sprites and a reduced-motion pose.
- Set the existing `IMAGE_GENERATION_TOOL=true` runtime environment override for Insiders and development builds. Stable is unchanged; runtime account/model access, policy, and permission checks remain authoritative.

**Scope:** Product changes, accessibility help, and regression coverage only. The developer mock command, sample photos, speed experiments, and exploratory fixtures have been removed. No new or modified Component Explorer fixture files or screenshot baselines are included. No new image-generation tool or SDK version bump.

**Runtime prerequisite:** The bundled Copilot runtime must contain the versioned `/v1/images/generations` endpoint fix, and that CAPI route must be deployed.

## How to Test

1. In an image-generation-capable Agents chat, attach an image and generate one or more images across multiple turns.
2. Verify generated outputs appear under **Generated Images** in Artifacts, separately from ordinary image/file artifacts, without duplicate entries.
3. Open an output from the transcript or Artifacts. Verify the carousel starts on that image and navigates through generated images and user attachments from the same conversation.
4. Expand a completed image dropdown. Check its duration, actual image size, and `Tokens -`; save separate generated images and verify the proposed filenames differ without changing their extensions.
5. Enable the chat pet and start image generation. It should paint while an image tool runs and return to its normal activity afterward. Confirm cancellation and reduced motion also behave correctly.
6. Watch the loading-to-image transition and response completion: resizing should start as soon as the image is ready, both dimensions should change continuously, and an empty turn summary should not shift the Copy toolbar or scroll position. Repeat with reduced motion/high contrast and a reopened conversation.
7. With a compatible runtime and authorized account, verify the image tool is available in Insiders. Stable must not receive the automatic environment override.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The changed read, per-image concurrency, provider boundary, full-body base64 decode, and expansion trigger are directly established. Exact byte volume depends on generated image sizes.
Findings.PerformanceResource: Remote resourceRead calls, base64 bytes, decoded image buffers, and IPC/network bandwidth
Findings.PerformanceScaling: One concurrent full-body read per referenced generated image; cost grows with both output count and total image byte size.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Excessive IPC/network I/O, expansion metadata latency, and transient memory pressure
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Before this PR, the dropdown had no image-size metadata and expanding it issued no file reads for referenced generated images.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: Expanding a completed image-generation dropdown now launches Promise.all over referenced outputs and calls fileService.readFile for each image whose byte length is not embedded.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: RIGHT line 217 adds the full-body read inside Promise.all for every referenced image lacking byteLength; no corresponding read existed before the metadata feature.
Findings.Title: Avoid downloading image bodies just to display their byte size
Findings.Impact: Expanding details for remote generated images can re-transfer megabytes that were already loaded for preview, delay the size field, and transiently allocate all referenced image bodies at once; multiple outputs fan out concurrently.
Findings.Evidence: The added line reads each complete image into a VSBuffer only to use value.byteLength. For vscode-agent-host resources, AgentHostFileSystemProvider.readFile performs a remote resourceRead with Base64 encoding and decodes the returned body, so this is a full cross-boundary transfer and allocation rather than a metadata query. The added test explicitly verifies the read starts on expansion.
Findings.Recommendation: Propagate optional byte length from tool/resource metadata into the reference part (or use resource stat when it reports a real size), and coalesce/cache any unavoidable fallback with the preview's existing load instead of issuing a separate concurrent body read per image.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The event source, synchronous derived dependency, always-observed toolbar path, and full-history loop are explicit. Only the exact history length and stream update count vary by user.
Findings.PerformanceResource: UI-thread CPU work and transient observable, array, map, action, and pill-entry objects
Findings.PerformanceScaling: O(total requests plus total response parts and surfaced artifacts) per response update; multiplied by the number of streamed updates in the active turn.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Increasing CPU/GC pressure and response-rendering latency for long conversations
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Before this PR, SessionArtifacts derived its sections only from persisted session artifacts/references and did not observe streamed chat response updates or scan the chat transcript.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: The new generated-images derivation subscribes to every response's onDidChange event and, when any response changes, walks every request and every response part again, then rebuilds all artifact sections and entries.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: The added RIGHT line 571 subscribes generatedImages to each response.onDidChange; the surrounding added loop then recomputes generated images for all requests and causes sectionsFor to rebuild the artifact presentation.
Findings.Title: Update generated-image pills incrementally instead of rescanning the transcript
Findings.Impact: In a long Agents conversation, each streamed chunk synchronously rescans the entire history and reallocates response signals, image arrays, maps, actions, and pill entries, adding UI-thread CPU/GC pressure and making response streaming increasingly janky as the conversation grows.
Findings.Evidence: ChatResponseModel forwards Response.onDidChangeValue to onDidChange, and Response._contentChanged fires that event for each non-quiet streamed content update. This added listener is inside a derivation that iterates model.getRequests().slice().reverse(), calls getGeneratedImageResources over each response.value, and feeds the newly allocated image list into buildSessionArtifactSections. SessionChatInputToolbar wires these sections into always-instantiated ChatInputPills, so the work is reachable while the Agents chat is open.
Findings.Recommendation: Keep a per-response cached/derived image list keyed by response and update only the response that changed, then aggregate cached lists when requests are added/removed. Avoid recreating event observables inside the whole-history derivation.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The source event fires directly from streamed content updates, the full-history loops precede cache lookup, and ChatArtifactsWidget keeps the derived value observed. Magnitude depends only on chat length and provider chunk cadence.
Findings.PerformanceResource: UI-thread CPU work plus transient event-observable, set, and aggregate-array allocations
Findings.PerformanceScaling: O(total response parts plus cached artifacts) for every streamed response update, rather than O(changed response) or only artifact-relevant transitions.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Higher CPU/GC pressure and lower response-streaming throughput as transcript size grows
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Before this PR, the derivation was invalidated by request-list/model changes and rule changes; ordinary streamed response content did not trigger a full-history artifact pass.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: The rules-artifacts derivation now observes every response change. Any streamed content event reruns the outer loop over all requests, scans every part to recount tool states, reconstructs the aggregate artifact list, and recreates response event observables even when every per-response extraction cache entry remains valid.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: The added RIGHT line 194 introduces response.onDidChange as a dependency of the one derivation that loops all requests; the new counts at lines 200-210 ensure every response part is revisited before cache hits can be recognized.
Findings.Title: Do not invalidate all artifact caches for every streamed chunk
Findings.Impact: Long chats with the artifacts widget pay history-wide synchronous CPU and allocation cost at token/progress cadence, reducing streaming throughput and causing UI jank even when a markdown chunk cannot change artifacts.
Findings.Evidence: Response._contentChanged emits onDidChangeValue for each non-quiet update, ChatResponseModel forwards that to response.onDidChange, and the added line subscribes the single history-wide derivation to it. The cache check occurs only after the code has iterated every response.value to compute partsLength, completedToolCount, and toolResultCount; afterward all cached artifacts are still deduplicated into a new allArtifacts array. ChatArtifactsWidget continuously observes artifactGroups after a session resource is set.
Findings.Recommendation: Factor extraction/signature tracking into a per-response derived/cache so only the changed response is rescanned, and aggregate cached results separately on request add/remove. If possible, invalidate on tool-result/completion transitions rather than generic response content events.

Scenarios.Scenario: Stream a new response in a long Agents conversation while the Artifacts pill is present above the input
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Each non-quiet response content update synchronously invalidates generatedImages; the toolbar's observed sections recompute before the observable transaction settles, so the full-history scan and pill reconstruction are on the response/UI update critical path.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Total historical requests, response parts, generated images, and streamed updates in the active turn.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Serialized on the UI thread for each response event; no coalescing or per-response isolation was found.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No per-response generated-image cache exists in SessionArtifacts. Every event recreates response signals and all image/pill presentation objects; warm history receives the same scan as cold history.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: ChatResponseModel forwards content changes to onDidChange, the added dependency is explicit, and the derivation loops the full model history.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact request counts and provider chunk cadence vary, but long-lived agent conversations and many streamed updates are normal; severity is medium rather than high because no timing trace is supplied.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable repeated-work regression: token-cadence O(history) synchronous CPU/GC was introduced where the pill previously consumed persisted artifacts only.

Scenarios.Scenario: Stream a response while ChatArtifactsWidget observes rule/generated artifacts
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The response event invalidates one history-wide derivation synchronously. Before downstream rendering can observe stable groups, all responses are traversed, tool states recounted, and cached artifacts reaggregated.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Total response parts and cached artifacts across the conversation multiplied by streamed content/progress updates.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Single-threaded and serialized per event; per-response extraction is cached, but invalidation and aggregation are not coalesced and still cover all responses.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Per-response extraction cache is warm when signatures do not change, but cache lookup occurs only after every response part is rescanned; aggregate sets/arrays and event observables are rebuilt on each update. No negative-cache issue was found.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the added response listener, pre-cache loops, and continuously observed widget autorun are directly traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Artifact-widget prevalence and transcript size vary; the mechanism remains certain, so this is medium severity.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable repeated-work regression: generic response updates now invalidate artifact work at token cadence instead of request/artifact transition cadence.

Scenarios.Scenario: Expand a completed image-generation dropdown to view duration, image size, and tokens
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Expansion itself renders immediately, but the requested image-size value remains pending until every referenced image body read completes; those reads are on the metadata completion path, not the initial disclosure animation path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: fileService.readFile of the entire referenced image; vscode-agent-host dispatches remote resourceRead(Base64) and decodes the body
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One call per referenced generated-image output lacking embedded byteLength; all calls for the expanded tool are launched together with Promise.all.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Expanding the dropdown did not read referenced image bodies because no size metadata was rendered.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Not required for the dropdown to open, but required for the byte-size field to resolve and competes for bandwidth/memory with visible image work.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of referenced outputs and their aggregate encoded/decoded byte size.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Unbounded within one tool output list via Promise.all; practical concurrency equals the number of referenced generated images in that tool result.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Embedded outputs use a computed byte length without decoding. Referenced outputs do not reuse a preview load, stat result, or coalesced body cache, so warm visible previews can still trigger another full read.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: tests establish expansion as the trigger and the provider implementation proves full remote transfer plus base64 decode.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Typical image count and size vary, but generated images are realistically megabytes and remote resources are supported; severity is low because the action is explicit and asynchronous.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable boundary fan-out: full bodies are fetched concurrently only to determine sizes.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open a generated image or attachment in the conversation carousel from transcript or artifact pills
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The service synchronously/async collects conversation metadata and embedded images before invoking the carousel command. URI-backed generated images and attachments are passed as URIs and load lazily in the carousel, so their file reads are not on collection assembly.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Fallback readFile when the clicked image cannot be found in any assembled section and no bytes were supplied
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one fallback read for the clicked resource; URI-backed images found in transcript/additional sections avoid it.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same single-image fallback read existed; the PR broadens section discovery and makes new URI-backed entries lazy.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Blocks opening only in the single-image fallback case.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Conversation item/image count and additional artifact image count after URI-key deduplication.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Collection traversal is serialized; no new boundary fan-out for referenced images. Additional-image deduplication is repeated linear search but realistic image cardinality is bounded and not reportable.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Embedded images remain in-memory data. URI-backed entries defer loading to the carousel; no new collection-level cache was added, but the changed behavior avoids eager reads.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for call flow and lazy URI behavior.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Very image-heavy conversations could expose quadratic additional-image lookup CPU, but realistic effective cardinality and one-click frequency do not support a finding.
Scenarios.Verdict: No regression reported; the changed boundary placement is neutral or beneficial.

Scenarios.Scenario: Reveal a generated image and animate the chat pet while image generation runs
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Image readiness starts one canvas/CSS reveal whose frame callback updates geometry; pet state checks the active response on response/tool observable changes and paints one bundled sprite animation. Neither path crosses subprocess, IPC, filesystem, database, or network boundaries after assets are loaded.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Generated previews visible simultaneously, canvas pixel dimensions, animation frames, and current-response part count.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One reveal animation per generated preview and one pet animation for the active widget; browser animation clocks serialize frame callbacks. The pet scans only the current response and short-circuits on the first active image tool.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Image samples/canvas data are per reveal; pet sprite sources use the existing bundled asset path. No unbounded retained cache or cleanup loss was found.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for changed animation flow; low evidence of negative magnitude.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Large preview dimensions and overlapping generations increase canvas work, but the diff shortens/skips the loading prefix and did not establish a regression over the previous reveal.

Scenarios.Scenario: Start or restart the Copilot runtime and map live/restored image-generation events
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Existing runtime startup constructs the subprocess environment and launches the same subprocess; event mapping performs constant-time timestamp parsing and metadata propagation.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Launch/restart the Copilot runtime with IMAGE_GENERATION_TOOL=true in non-Stable builds
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One existing subprocess launch per startup/restart; the diff changes one environment value only.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The runtime subprocess was already launched with the assembled environment; it simply lacked this override.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Subprocess startup remains on the existing runtime startup path; no additional process or IPC round trip is added.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of image tool calls/events; one metadata calculation per completion.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Unchanged existing startup/restart sequencing; timestamp calculations are synchronous constant-time work per image tool completion.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: None material for the added constant-time metadata work.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass across all 59 changed files and all patch pages. Reported two token-cadence full-history artifact rescans and one per-image remote full-body metadata read; reviewed carousel laziness, reveal/pet rendering, save paths, event mapping, and runtime startup without additional findings.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
